name: Tahiti Reed Warbler
rangeDescription: Tahiti (society islands)
description: A large, slender warbler with a disproportionately long bill, short wings, and a long tail. Face and eyebrow yellowish-buff with a dark eye-stripe and a pale throat.

name: White-winged Potoo
rangeDescription: Northern amazonia (northeastern peru and northern brazil) and eastern brazil (bahia and espírito santo)
description: Uncommon, rarely seen potoo, active only at night. If found during the day, large white wing patches are key to identification.

name: Ludwig's Bustard
rangeDescription: Far southwestern angola to namibia, southwestern botswana, and south africa
description: A large-to-medium-sized bustard with a dull orangish nape and hind neck, and dark gray-brown fore neck and face. Female and juvenile are smaller than male and paler on the face and throat.

name: Jerdon's Minivet
rangeDescription: Plains of central myanmar
description: Dainty minivet of dry forests, scrubland, and cultivation edge in Myanmar’s central Irrawaddy plains. Male is black and white, with an orange patch on the chest.

name: Sakhalin Grasshopper Warbler
rangeDescription: Sakhalin, southern kuril islands, and hokkaido; winters in philippines
description: A nondescript songbird that skulks in taiga undergrowth, where very difficult to see well. Breeds on Hokkaido, Sakhalin Island, and the Kuril Islands.

name: White-throated Robin
rangeDescription: Türkiye, southern caucasus, and levant eastward to iran, and from southern kazakhstan and tajikistan to western and northern afghanistan; possibly also central uzbekistan; winters in northeastern and eastern africa
description: Large, long-billed robin that spends much of its time on the ground with tail cocked. The male has bluish upperparts, a dark face, a white supercilium, a broad black tail, and bright orange underparts.

name: Imperial Woodpecker
rangeDescription: Sierra madre occidental of western mexico; probably extinct
description: Learn about Imperial Woodpecker: explore photos, sounds, and observations collected by birders around the world.

name: Western Kingbird
rangeDescription: Breeds western north america; winters southern mexico to costa rica and (?) panama
description: Fairly large yellow-bellied flycatcher; common and widespread in western North America. Rather pale gray head with weakly contrasting whitish throat and breast, and lemon-yellow belly.

name: Kirk's White-eye
rangeDescription: Grand comoro island
description: A small, sharp-billed warbler-like bird. Note the completely yellow underparts and the broad white spectacles around the eye.

name: Guatemalan Tyrannulet
rangeDescription: Highlands of southern mexico (chiapas), guatemala and western el salvador
description: Small, drab tyrannulet found in the highlands of southern Mexico, Guatemala, and western El Salvador. Fairly inconspicuous; usually found as singles or pairs in middle to upper levels of forests, plantations, and second-growth.

name: Crested Ant-Tanager
rangeDescription: Western andes of colombia (antioquia to cauca)
description: Unmistakable; dull red tanager with grayer flanks and obvious bright red crest. Sexes similar; males have longer crest.

name: Common Sandpiper
rangeDescription: Palearctic; winters to southern africa, central asia, philippines, and australia
description: Small bicolored sandpiper which often bobs its tail in a distinctively wagtail-like manner. Plain brown with white underparts; distinguished from bulkier and rounder-headed Green Sandpiper by a prominent white spur at the shoulder.

name: White-fronted Ground-Tyrant
rangeDescription: Andes of southern peru (ancash) to western bolivia and far northern chile
description: Largest ground-tyrant, usually identified readily by (relatively) big size and high Andean range. Usually seen as singles or pairs foraging on bogs, but also ranges into adjacent rocky puna habitats.

name: Brown-capped Tyrannulet
rangeDescription: Costa rica to western colombia, northwestern ecuador, and northwestern venezuela
description: Tiny short-tailed flycatcher. Yellow below with white eyebrow that wraps around the forehead.

name: Upland Buzzard
rangeDescription: Open steppes and montane slopes of eastern asia
description: A large raptor of expansive open spaces such as steppe, pastures, and semi-deserts. Perches visibly on utility poles and snags.

name: Rondonia Bushbird
rangeDescription: South-central amazonian brazil, in rondônia, southern amazonas, and northern mato grosso
description: Large antbird with a very distinctive, robust upturned bill. Males are all black and females are chestnut with a black throat patch.

name: Black-throated Spinetail
rangeDescription: Coastal mountains of northern venezuela (aragua to distrito federal)
description: Bright rufous bird with a long, spiky tail and black lores and throat. Sexes similar; juvenile lacks black throat.

name: Natal Spurfowl
rangeDescription: Zambia and mozambique to cape province
description: A medium-size brownish francolin with distinctive yellow nostrils and a bright orange-red bill and legs. The back is mottled brown, and the underpart feathers are edged brown and white, giving it a marbled scaled appearance.

name: Sora
rangeDescription: Southern alaska to northern baja california and southern usa; winters to west indies and northern south america
description: Fairly small rail; short yellow bill, black face, and gray neck distinctive. Found in marshes with grasses or reeds; generally shy but often seen foraging at the edge of shallow water.

name: Glaucous-winged Gull
rangeDescription: Bering sea to northwestern oregon; winters to japan and northwestern mexico
description: Large, stocky gull of the North Pacific. Generally fairly pale and uniform-looking; at all ages, note wingtips and back are approximately the same color.
